svg.title: Which findings in a child's history should the nurse identify as contraindications to taking a rectal temperature? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Two reasons, and every right answer is one of them. Vagal stimulation — a rectal probe can trigger a vagal response and drop the heart rate, which a child with a cardiac condition can least afford. And breaching the mucosa — a child on chemotherapy or otherwise immunosuppressed may be neutropenic and thrombocytopenic, so a small tear becomes bleeding and a route for bacteria. Diarrhea (and fecal impaction) rules it out too: the reading is unreliable and the tissue is already irritated. Respiratory trouble and vomiting are not contraindications — they are reasons to avoid the oral route, which is the swap people make by mistake. Axillary works at any age. Oral waits until the child can hold their mouth closed, about 5 to 6 years .
